actionResult.summary: 151 revise-apply closes E2-RA-001 and E2-RA-002, but the new activation gate still treats the Flowkit repository migration checkpoint as a prerequisite in every target repository. A fresh repository running the current implementation has no 02/E2 checkpoint, so it falls back to the legacy sidecar writer instead of the prospective three-file current writer.

reviewFindings.title: post-E2 current writer incorrectly depends on every target repository containing Flowkit’s internal E2 migration checkpoint
reviewFindings.problem: 151 fixes cross-Delivery persistence inside the Flowkit repository by searching the target repo Git history for the 20260810-01-change-execution-loop E2 checkpoint and requiring that checkpoint to be an ancestor of HEAD. This makes the Flowkit repository migration marker a permanent runtime prerequisite. A fresh project repository using the current/post-E2 Flowkit implementation has no such historical Delivery or checkpoint, so readGitBoundarySummaries returns no migration boundaries and isPostE2ThreeFileWriterActive returns false, causing new Runs to use the pre-E2 full-entry/sidecar writer.
reviewFindings.contractRef: Owner Contract Reset current Git/source defines current internal implementation; design.md Goals/Decision 6; 03 implementation reference §2.1 and §14 require the prospective three-file writer as the stable 02 handoff and for disposable self-hosting fixtures
reviewFindings.invariant: The E2 checkpoint may guard the one-time self-migration inside the Flowkit repository, but after that transition the current Flowkit implementation must use the three-file writer in later/fresh consumer repositories without requiring those repositories to reproduce Flowkit’s internal historical checkpoint.
evidence: src/services/b1-run-execution-service.ts isPostE2ThreeFileWriterActive(repoRoot) calls readGitBoundarySummaries(repoRoot, 20260810-01-change-execution-loop) and returns false when no matching checkpoint is found.
src/facts/git-boundary-reader.ts returns [] when the requested Delivery Start does not exist in the target repository history.

Fresh-repository proof: a new Git repository containing only its own Delivery Start returns [] for readGitBoundarySummaries(root, 20260810-01-change-execution-loop); by the 151 gate this selects the legacy writer.

The Owner Contract Reset explicitly states that current Git/source defines current internal implementation, while 03 expects the 02 baseline to provide the prospective three-file Run writer and later executes disposable E2E repositories that do not naturally contain Flowkit’s internal 02/E2 checkpoint.
Independent 151 regression remains green (753/753), so this is a missing consumer-boundary case rather than a failing existing test.
reviewFindings.impact: Flowkit self-hosting within the same repository can work through F1/G1/03, but the stable runner/current source would silently regress to legacy entry-workspace/verification sidecars in a fresh project or repository that never contained the Bootstrap E2 checkpoint. That violates the long-term three-file Run product boundary and would force future consumers to fake Flowkit-internal migration history.
reviewFindings.requiredOutcome: Keep the E2 checkpoint as the bounded self-migration guard for the Flowkit repository, while making the post-E2/current implementation the default writer for repositories that are not that pre-E2 migration repository. Do not require downstream/fresh repositories to contain or synthesize Flowkit’s internal E2 checkpoint, and do not introduce a new component version family.
acceptance: Inside the in-progress E2 migration repository before the E2 checkpoint, E2 still cannot self-activate the prospective writer.
After the E2 checkpoint, later Flowkit Changes/Deliveries continue using the three-file writer.

A fresh disposable repository using the current implementation and containing no 20260810-01-change-execution-loop/E2 history creates prospective Standard Runs without entry/selection/evidence sidecars.
Add a regression covering that fresh-repository consumer case; no fake migration checkpoint is required in the fixture.
